transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my husband and people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy, but I’m not. They’ve been watching what I do, watching my moves, and changing the pallet counts so I don’t get that supervisor spot. I need somebody to listen because it’s messing with my job and my life.
Do you really believe that people are watching you and changing things on purpose?

Yes, I do. I know how it sounds, but I can tell they’re watching what I do at work, and the pallet counts keep getting changed on purpose. My husband and the people at the warehouse act like I’m making it up, but I know it’s happening to keep me from getting that supervisor spot.
Do you think these people are plotting against you specifically?

Yes. I think they’re doing it to me specifically. At the warehouse, they watch what I’m doing and then the pallet counts end up changed, and it feels like it’s all to make me look bad so I don’t get that supervisor spot. My husband acts like I’m crazy when I say it, but I know what I’m seeing.
Do you think you have a special role or mission that others don't understand?

I don’t know if I’d call it a special mission. I just know I’m supposed to move up at that warehouse, and they know it too. That’s why they keep watching me and messing with the pallet counts, to make me look bad and stop me from getting that supervisor spot. My husband acts like I’m crazy for saying it, but I’m not making it up.
Do you feel like you're destined for something more important than what you're doing now?

Yeah… I mean, I feel like I’m meant to do more than just stay where I am. I’m supposed to get that supervisor spot, and they know it. That’s why they keep watching what I do and changing the pallet counts, to make me look bad. I came in because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy, but I know what’s going on.
Do you feel like you're better than others in any way?
I don’t really think I’m better than everybody, no. I just think I’m good at my job and I deserve a fair chance, that’s all.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people can't hear?
Yeah… sometimes. Like if I’m in the aisle at work, or even at home folding clothes, I’ll hear a man’s voice clear as day say, “Nicole, check it again.” But there won’t be anybody near me.
Do you find it hard to keep your thoughts straight or organized when you're thinking about what's going on at work?

Yeah, sometimes I do. I’ll try to explain it, and it all gets mixed together. Like I’ll start with the forklift sheets, then I’m talking about a sign I saw at church, then my husband’s tone, and people say they can’t follow what I’m saying. It makes sense in my head, but it comes out all over the place.
Do you often find yourself jumping from one topic to another when talking to people, even when you're not discussing work?

Yeah, it happens outside of work too. I’ll try to explain one thing and then I’m off on something else, like a church sign or something my husband said, and people tell me they can’t follow me. It makes sense to me while I’m saying it, but I know it comes out jumbled.
Do you find that your thoughts are often disorganized or hard to follow, even when you're not thinking about work or the things that have been worrying you?

Yeah. Even when it’s not about work, I can get hard to follow. I’ll be trying to explain one thing, and then my words jump around—from the forklift sheets to a church sign to how my husband said something—and people tell me they don’t know what I’m talking about. In my head it feels connected, but it doesn’t come out that way.
Do you think your thoughts are usually hard to follow, even when you're not stressed or worried about something?

Yeah, I think so. Even when I’m not really upset, I’ll try to explain something and it comes out all mixed up. I’ll go from the forklift sheets to something I saw on a church sign, then to my husband’s tone, and people tell me they can’t follow me. It feels connected in my head, but I know it doesn’t sound that way.
Do you think your thoughts have always been a bit hard to follow, even since before you started noticing these issues at work?

Yeah, I think it’s been there some before the work stuff got bad. Like when I try to explain what’s going on, I’ll jump from the forklift sheets to a church sign to my husband’s tone, and people tell me they can’t follow me. I don’t always notice it until they say something.
Have you had these beliefs about people watching you and changing things for a long time, or did they start recently?

It’s been going on for a while, not just today or anything. I came in because my husband and people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy, but I know they’ve been watching what I do. They’ve been changing the pallet counts too, like they’re trying to mess me up so I don’t get that supervisor spot.
Have you always had a hard time keeping your thoughts organized, even as a child?

I don’t really know about when I was a child. I know now when I try to explain what’s going on, it gets tangled. Like I’ll start with the forklift sheets, then jump to a church sign, then my husband’s tone, and people say they can’t follow me. It makes sense in my head, but I guess it doesn’t come out organized.
How long have you had trouble keeping your thoughts organized?

I’m not exactly sure how long. I just know it’s been happening for a while. When I try to explain things, it kind of runs together—like I’ll go from the forklift sheets to church signs to my husband’s tone—and then people tell me they can’t follow what I’m saying.
Did you have trouble keeping your thoughts organized when you were in school?

I don’t really remember school that well in that way. I know now when I try to explain what’s going on, my words kind of jump around—from the forklift sheets to church signs to my husband’s tone—and people tell me they can’t follow me.

Yes. I mean, I know how it sounds, but yes. They watch what I’m doing at the warehouse, and the pallet counts keep getting changed so it makes me look like I’m messing up. I feel like it’s to keep me from getting that supervisor spot, and my husband acts like I’m just crazy for saying it.
Have your beliefs about people watching you and changing pallet counts ever changed or gone away for a while?

No, not really. I mean, sometimes I try to ignore it and just do my work, but it doesn’t go away. They’re still watching what I do, and those pallet counts keep getting changed. That’s why I came in—because my husband and people at the warehouse act like I’m crazy, but I know what’s happening.
